title: "Design Lab: S3-Like Object Storage"

# Design Lab: S3-Like Object Storage

Build a Go object service with bucket/key addressing, immutable versions, and metadata stored separately from bytes. “S3-like” describes the exercise's object model; the lab does not implement S3 authentication or wire compatibility.

## Begin with atomic publication

Expose `PUT /buckets/{bucket}/objects/{key...}`, `GET`, and `DELETE`. Authorize the bucket and key before storage access. Treat object keys as opaque identifiers: map them to generated storage IDs rather than concatenating them into local paths.

Store metadata `(bucket, key, version, blob_id, length, sha256, state)`. A PUT streams bytes to a temporary blob, enforces a size limit, calculates its checksum, and closes/syncs it under the stated durability policy. Publish committed metadata only after the blob is complete. GET returns only committed versions.

The streaming core is a fragment within the upload handler; import `crypto/sha256`, `io`, and `fmt`:

```go
h := sha256.New()
n, err := io.Copy(io.MultiWriter(tmpFile, h), io.LimitReader(body, maxBytes+1))
if err != nil {
	return err
}
if n > maxBytes {
	return fmt.Errorf("object too large")
}
sum := h.Sum(nil)
```

Validate `maxBytes` before this fragment, and remove the temporary object on every failed path. A checksum detects corruption; it does not authenticate the caller. Do not assume an external provider's ETag is always a content hash.

## Multipart and concurrency

Add upload sessions with unique part numbers, checksums, and an expiry. Completion validates the exact ordered part manifest and publishes one object version transactionally. Repeating completion returns the same result. An expired upload is ineligible for completion before garbage collection removes its parts. The [S3 multipart documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html) provides a real API reference for this lifecycle.

Support conditional replacement using a version precondition so two writers cannot silently lose updates. DELETE creates a tombstone or removes the current metadata pointer according to your versioning contract. Garbage collection must use references and a grace period; a concurrent uploader must not lose its newly written blob.

## Distribution and recovery evidence

For a local milestone, run one metadata store and one disk. For a replicated milestone, define how many independent copies must be durable before success and how repairs verify content. Erasure coding is a later experiment with explicit recovery and write-amplification measurements.

Kill the service after blob creation and before metadata commit: an orphan may remain, but GET must never expose a partial object. Test missing blobs, checksum mismatch, duplicate multipart completion, concurrent conditional writes, and abandoned-upload cleanup. Report orphan bytes, repair backlog, upload latency, and failed checksum checks. The [video](06-video-platform.qmd) and [file-sync](07-file-sync.qmd) labs reuse this publication boundary.
